---
title: Search with Elasticsearch
---

SearcherKit can use an Elasticsearch index as a private knowledge base. The
agent searches the index for relevant passages, optionally fetches complete
documents, and then answers from the retrieved evidence.

```bash
question -> LLM -> search -> Elasticsearch matches
                -> visit  -> indexed document
                -> LLM -> final answer
```

This guide starts with BM25 because it needs only Elasticsearch. Vector and
hybrid retrieval are covered after the basic pipeline is working.

### Install SearcherKit

SearcherKit requires Python 3.12 or later. Install the package in a virtual
environment:

:::: {.panel-tabset}
#### pip

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ml-stat-Sustech/searcherkit.git
cd searcherkit
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e .
```

#### uv

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ml-stat-Sustech/searcherkit.git
cd searcherkit
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
uv pip install -e .
```
::::

You need a running Elasticsearch service and an OpenAI-compatible LLM
endpoint. Check [Elasticsearch Documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.19/search-with-elasticsearch.html) to setup your own elasticsearch service. 

With a valid elasticsearch endpoint, confirm that Elasticsearch is reachable before continuing:
```bash
curl http://your.elasticsearch.endpoint:port
```

### Prepare an index

The default installation includes the Elasticsearch client. To build an index with SearcherKit's deployment plugins, install the indexing dependencies:

```bash
pip install -e ".[indexing]"
```

An Elasticsearch source works with an existing index. SearcherKit includes
deployment plugins for MediaWiki dumps and BrowseComp Plus corpora. Both create
documents with `title`, `text`, `url`, and `links` fields.

To index a local MediaWiki dump for BM25 search:

```bash
searcher plugins deploy local-wiki \
  --wiki_dump_path data/wiki.xml.bz2 \
  --es_host http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  --index_name wiki_local \
  --overwrite
```

To index BrowseComp Plus instead:

```bash
searcher plugins deploy browsecomp-plus \
  --dataset_path data/browsecomp_plus_corpus.jsonl \
  --es_host http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  --index_name browsecomp_plus \
  --overwrite
```

`--overwrite` deletes and recreates an index with the same name. Omit it when
you do not want an existing index replaced.

If you manage the index outside SearcherKit, map the source fields in the
configuration below. At minimum, the fields in `search_fields` must be
searchable. The field used by `document_id_field` and `fetch_field` must
identify a document unambiguously.

### Configure the environment

Set the LLM connection values in the shell that will run SearcherKit:

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Bash

```bash
export LLM_MODEL="YOUR_MODEL"
export LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
export LLM_BASE_URL="https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
```

#### PowerShell

```powershell
$env:LLM_MODEL = "YOUR_MODEL"
$env:LLM_API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"
$env:LLM_BASE_URL = "https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
To keep these values across terminal sessions, put them in a `.env` file in
the directory where you run SearcherKit:

```dotenv
LLM_MODEL=YOUR_MODEL
LLM_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY
LLM_BASE_URL=https://your-endpoint.example/v1
```

SearcherKit loads `.env` by default. Values already defined in the shell take
precedence.
:::

### Create a BM25 search configuration

Create `elasticsearch_search.yaml` in the repository root:

```yaml
defaults:
  - _self_

agent:
  llm_client:
    type: openai
    model: ${oc.env:LLM_MODEL}
    api_key: ${oc.env:LLM_API_KEY,EMPTY}
    base_url: ${oc.env:LLM_BASE_URL}
    default_kwargs:
      temperature: 0.2
      max_completion_tokens: 4096

  parser:
    type: upstream

  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: knowledge_base
      hosts: [http://127.0.0.1:9200]
      index: wiki_local
      search_fields: [title^2, text]
      title_field: title
      text_field: text
      url_field: url
      document_id_field: url
      fetch_field: url
      vector_search_mode: bm25
      highlight: true
      highlight_fragment_size: 256
      highlight_number_of_fragments: 5
      snippet_chars: 2048
      request_timeout: 30
      es_max_concurrency: 8

  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      description: Search the private knowledge base for relevant evidence.
      source: [knowledge_base]
      response_char_limit: 20000
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      description: Read a document returned by search using its URL.
      source: [knowledge_base]
      response_char_limit: 50000

  system_prompt: |
    You answer questions using evidence from the private knowledge base.
    Search before answering, and visit the most relevant documents when the
    search snippets do not contain enough context. Do not invent evidence.

  max_turn: 16
  max_tokens: 32768
  max_tokens_prompt_margin: 4096
  max_tokens_prompt: |
    The context limit is close. Stop calling tools and answer from the evidence already collected.
  llm_retry_config:
    max_tries: 3
  tool_retry_config:
    max_tries: 3
    exceptions:
      - pkg://searcherkit.common.errors:RecoverableError

output_path: outputs/elasticsearch-search-tui

logging:
  global_file: ${output_path}/run.log
  trace:
    enabled: true
    dir: ${output_path}/traces
    format: text
    level: DEBUG
    filename_template: "{sample_id}_{trace_id}.log"
```

The source name is internal to SearcherKit. The `search` and `visit` tools use
`source: [knowledge_base]` to select that source. For an index without a stable
URL field, remove `document_id_field` and `fetch_field`; search results will use
the Elasticsearch `_id`, and `visit` will fetch by `_id`.

### Validate and start the TUI

Validate the configuration before connecting to the services:

```bash
searcher inspect --config-path elasticsearch_search.yaml
```

Then start the interactive interface:

```bash
searcher tui --config-path elasticsearch_search.yaml
```

Use `/tool-detail` to inspect queries, result snippets, document identifiers,
and fetched content. Interactive records and trace logs are written under
`outputs/elasticsearch-search-tui/interactive` and
`outputs/elasticsearch-search-tui/traces`.

For a non-interactive smoke test, pass one question directly:

```bash
searcher tui --config-path elasticsearch_search.yaml \
  --query "What topics are covered by this knowledge base?"
```

### Enable vector or hybrid retrieval

Vector search embeds each query and compares it with a dense-vector field in
the index. Hybrid search combines vector retrieval with BM25. Both modes require:

- a dense-vector field populated during indexing;
- the same embedding model and vector dimension at indexing and query time;
- an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint available to SearcherKit.

For example, build a Qwen3 vector index from a wiki dump:

```bash
searcher plugins deploy local-wiki \
  --wiki_dump_path data/wiki.xml.bz2 \
  --es_host http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  --index_name wiki_qwen3 \
  --dense-vector \
  --model_name Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B \
  --embedding_dim 4096 \
  --prompt_strategy qwen3 \
  --overwrite
```

Check the model's actual embedding dimension rather than assuming `4096` for a
different model or configuration.

Replace the Elasticsearch source in the YAML with:

```yaml
  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: knowledge_base
      hosts: [http://127.0.0.1:9200]
      index: wiki_qwen3
      search_fields: [title^2, text]
      title_field: title
      text_field: text
      url_field: url
      document_id_field: url
      fetch_field: url
      vector_search_mode: hybrid
      vector_field: text_vector
      embedding_model: Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B
      embedding_base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8004/v1
      embedding_api_key: EMPTY
      embedding_prefix: |-
        Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query
        Query:
      highlight: true
      highlight_fragment_size: 256
      highlight_number_of_fragments: 5
      snippet_chars: 2048
      es_max_concurrency: 8
      embedding_max_concurrency: 8
      embedding_retry_config:
        max_tries: 3
```

::: {.callout-tip}
`highlight: true` is valid with `bm25` and `hybrid`. Set `highlight: false` for
pure `vector` mode because Elasticsearch highlighting depends on a text query.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
Some embedding servers apply a query instruction themselves. Configure
`embedding_prefix` only when the server does not, so that the instruction is
applied exactly once. Document embeddings must use the model's document prompt
convention; query embeddings must use its query prompt convention.
:::

### Common failures and solutions

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Connection refused or timeout | Elasticsearch host, port, TLS settings, proxy, firewall, and service health |
| Index not found | The configured `index` name and the result of `curl http://127.0.0.1:9200/_cat/indices?v` |
| Search returns no matches | `search_fields`, analyzers, indexed content, and whether the query language matches the corpus |
| `visit` cannot find a result | `document_id_field` and `fetch_field`; use `_id` by omitting both when no stable field exists |
| Vector dimension error | Index mapping dimension versus the embedding endpoint's returned vector dimension |
| Authentication failure | Elasticsearch `client_kwargs`, embedding API key, or LLM API key |
| Vector mode rejects the config | `embedding_model`, `embedding_api_key`, `vector_field`, and `highlight: false` |
| Model rejects tool calls | Model chat template, provider tool-call support, and parser configuration |

For the complete source field reference and model-visible tool schemas, see
[Sources and Tools](../03-customizing/03-sources-and-tools.qmd). For TUI controls
and saved record behavior, see
[Use the Interactive TUI](../04-interface/02-use-the-interactive-tui.qmd).
